subject: Recap: FinHealth discovery \n\nPrivate/VPC requirements
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Patel <sara.patel@finhealth.com>
Cc: Tom Lambert <tom.lambert@finhealth.com>
Date: 2026-06-20T10:15:00-07:00
Subject: Recap: FinHealth discovery 
Private/VPC requirements

Hi Sara / Tom,

Thanks again for the intro call this morning — great to meet the FinHealth team. Per our discussion, here's a short recap and suggested next steps so we can align on a technical deep-dive.

Key pain points you called out:
- Processing regulated patient financial data in an environment that must remain within their VPC and meet strict audit controls.
- Current vendor latency/costs when running OCR/parsing at scale (batch jobs + near real-time workflows).
- Need for customer-managed keys and clear data residency controls for compliance.

Current stack / constraints you mentioned:
- Core platform in AWS (us-east-1), using a private VPC and strict egress policies.
- On-prem data stores for certain PHI-adjacent datasets; limited network connectivity to cloud.
- Procurement requires SOC2 + encryption-in-transit and at-rest with KMS/HSM integration.

Success criteria we captured:
1) Private deployment option (VPC or on-prem) that can be audited and integrates with your KMS.
2) Predictable latency for near-real-time inference (<200ms p95 for short prompts) or a clear fall-back plan.
3) Clear SLAs/controls around data retention, audit logs, and access control.

Next steps:
- I'll share a short private overview deck and our security questionnaire (attached).
- Schedule a technical deep-dive with your infra/security team + our SE (Vivek) and security lead (Lauren).
- Procurement: we'll provide baseline SOW language and an estimated pricing band for Dedicated/Private options.

Attachments: redwood-private-overview.pdf (overview, deployment options), security-questionnaire-FinHealth.docx (stub)

Proposed times for technical deep-dive: Wed 2026-06-23 10:00–11:00 ET or Thu 2026-06-24 14:00–15:00 ET — let me know what works.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0147

From: Sara Patel <sara.patel@finhealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Lambert <tom.lambert@finhealth.com>, procurement@finhealth.com
Date: 2026-06-20T11:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Recap: FinHealth discovery — Private/VPC requirements

Hi Marissa — thanks for the recap and for capturing everything so clearly. A few clarifications from our side: 

- The air-gap/on-prem constraint applies to about ~15% of our dataset (historical PHI-adjacent records). Those workflows need an on-prem or isolated-hosting path; the rest can live in our VPC.
- Customer-managed keys are mandatory for anything considered PHI-adjacent; we use AWS KMS with an external HSM for critical keys.
- Our security team will need to validate audit logs and the ability to push logs to our SIEM (Splunk) or ingest via S3.

Tom from infra is cc'd — Tom, can you confirm whether Wed 6/23 10 ET works for a 60m technical session? Also looped procurement for initial SOW requirements.

Thanks,
Sara Patel
Director of Product, FinHealth
sara.patel@finhealth.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Patel <sara.patel@finhealth.com>, Tom Lambert <tom.lambert@finhealth.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-06-20T12:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Recap: FinHealth discovery — Private/VPC requirements

Great — thanks Sara. Looping in Vivek (Solutions Engineering) and Lauren (Security) from our side to prepare for the technical session. Vivek / Lauren: brief context above — FinHealth requires a hybrid model (VPC + small on-prem air-gapped footprint), AWS KMS/HSM integration, Splunk log ingestion, and SOC2 evidence.

Vivek: can you prepare:
- Deployment options (VPC-only vs on-prem appliance vs hybrid) with trade-offs on latency/cost.
- Typical network diagram and required firewall rules for minimal connectivity (or steps for fully air-gapped evaluation).

Lauren: I attached our standard security questionnaire; if you can pre-populate the SOC2, encryption, retention, and logging answers we'll share with FinHealth ahead of the call.

I'll also open a HubSpot deal and share the Drive link (below) with all artifacts. If we get tentative calendar confirmation, we'll block the 60m window.

Drive: https://drive.google.com/finhealth/redwood-private-overview
HubSpot: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/1234567

Cheers,
Marissa

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Patel <sara.patel@finhealth.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-06-20T14:30:00-07:00
Subject: Redwood security questionnaire — FinHealth

Hi Sara / Marissa,

Attached is a pre-filled security questionnaire covering SOC2 posture, encryption (in-transit & at-rest), KMS/HSM integration notes, logging/retention, and our typical audit artifacts. This is a living doc; happy to walk through any sections during the technical session.

Attachment: security-questionnaire-FinHealth.docx (answers + evidence pointers)

A few high-level notes:
- We support customer-managed keys via AWS KMS and can integrate with external HSMs for key import.
- For air-gapped/on-prem use-cases we provide an on-prem package and an acceptance test plan; network egress can be restricted to a management plane controlled by the customer.
- Audit logs can be exported to S3 or pushed to SIEM via our log-forwarder; we keep an immutable audit trail for at least 90 days by default (configurable).

Please let me know any questions and confirm the call time so we can prepare diagrams and runbooks.

Best,
Lauren Bishop
Head of Security, Redwood Inference
lauren.bishop@redwood.ai
